plot01_hist_value.title: Distribution of Team Valuations ($ Billions)
plot01_hist_value.inference: The valuation distribution exhibits a strong positive (right) skew, with over 60% of top-50 teams clustered between $2.4B and $3.5B. A distinct elite tier (Cowboys, Yankees, Knicks) pulls the right tail above $5.0B, creating a notable gap between the median ($3.2B) and top performers.

plot02_box_value_sport.title: Team Valuation by Sport Category
plot02_box_value_sport.inference: European Soccer maintains the highest median valuation (.10B) and mean valuation (.84B) due to exclusive global brand equity, while the NFL maintains the largest market share (52% of top 50, 26 teams) and a highly consistent valuation floor (median .07B, IQR .665B) anchored by collective media agreements and strict salary cap parity. Basketball exhibits the widest valuation dispersion (IQR .95B) between marquee big-market teams (.6B-.0B) and small-market franchises.

plot03_bar_top10.title: Top 10 Most Valuable Sports Franchises Worldwide
plot03_bar_top10.inference: Dallas Cowboys claim the pinnacle ($5.70B), followed by New York Yankees ($5.25B) and New York Knicks ($5.00B). American franchises capture 7 of the top 10 positions, while European football giants Barcelona ($4.76B) and Real Madrid ($4.75B) anchor the global contingent.

plot04_donut_sport_share.title: Share of Top 50 Franchises by Sport
plot04_donut_sport_share.inference: American Football (NFL) accounts for an overwhelming 52.0% (26 of 50) of the globe's premier sports properties. Basketball (NBA) holds 18.0%, Soccer accounts for 18.0%, and Baseball (MLB) represents 12.0%, proving the commercial heft of US gridiron football.

plot05_scatter_price_vs_val.title: Acquisition Price Paid vs. Current Valuation ($B)
plot05_scatter_price_vs_val.inference: Franchises acquired at modest baseline prices (<$300M in the 20th century) show dramatic multi-thousand-percent capital gains. Newer transactions above $1.5B show contemporary institutional pricing, resulting in higher nominal capital outlays.

plot06_corr_heatmap.title: Pearson Correlation Matrix of Financial Metrics
plot06_corr_heatmap.inference: Years Held exhibits a strong negative correlation with Year Purchased (-1.00) and a moderate negative correlation with Price Paid (-0.57), verifying inflation and skyrocketing franchise values over successive ownership eras. Value correlates weakly with 5-year growth (-0.04), indicating mature market resilience.

plot07_violin_growth_sport.title: 5-Year Valuation Growth Rate Distribution by Sport
plot07_violin_growth_sport.inference: Soccer and select NBA teams show wide, tall violin profiles with long tails extending past 150%-200% growth (e.g., PSG at 207%, Liverpool at 165%), driven by international branding. The NFL exhibits a compact bell distribution clustered tightly around 50%-65%.

plot08_pairplot.title: Multivariate Pairwise Feature Relationships by Sport
plot08_pairplot.inference: Bivariate distributions demonstrate distinct cluster boundaries: Soccer occupies the high-growth perimeter, MLB occupies moderate value and moderate acquisition prices, and NFL dominates the central high-density valuation core.

plot09_line_vintage_trend.title: Average Franchise Valuation & Growth by Purchase Decade
plot09_line_vintage_trend.inference: Franchises held since the 1920s-1970s maintain remarkably resilient multi-billion-dollar values. Meanwhile, franchises bought during the 2000s and 2010s show accelerated recent 5-year percentage valuation gains due to modernization and global streaming monetization.

plot10_qq_density.title: Normality Diagnostics (Q-Q & Density)
plot10_qq_density.inference: The Q-Q plot exhibits pronounced convex curvature at upper quantiles, confirming heavy positive skewness. This violates standard Gaussian assumptions, strongly justifying nonparametric and tree-based data mining methods (such as FP-Growth and Naive Bayes discretization).

plot11_stacked_sport_country.title: Geographic Country Distribution by Sport Discipline
plot11_stacked_sport_country.inference: American Football, Baseball, and Basketball are 100% geographically concentrated in the USA. Conversely, the Soccer category is partitioned across the UK (5 teams), Spain (2 teams), Germany (1 team), and France (1 team), illustrating Europe's polycentric soccer landscape.

plot12_bubble_valuation.title: Valuation vs. 5-Year Growth Rate (Bubble Size = Years Held)
plot12_bubble_valuation.inference: Franchises held for decades (largest bubbles) occupy the upper valuation plateau with steady compound gains. Outlying high-growth properties (e.g., Golden State Warriors, LA Rams, PSG) are medium-sized bubbles purchased in the modern era, capturing rapid franchise re-evaluations.

plot13_confusion_matrix_nb.title: Naive Bayes Valuation Tier Confusion Matrix
plot13_confusion_matrix_nb.inference: Categorical Naive Bayes achieves 40.0% test accuracy on the holdout partition (N=10) using non-collinear categorical predictors (League, Growth_Tier, Price_Tier, Tenure_Tier). Misclassifications reflect small-sample test variance and non-linear valuation premiums, with the classifier establishing dominant probabilistic indicators linking low acquisition prices and moderate tenure to high current valuations.

plot14_agnes_dendrogram.title: AGNES Hierarchical Clustering Dendrogram (Ward Linkage)
plot14_agnes_dendrogram.inference: The dendrogram evaluated without collinear year duplication exhibits strong cophenetic correlation (0.7351) and silhouette score (0.3764), partitioning franchises into 3 macro-clusters: Recent High-Capital Takeovers (7 teams), Hyper-Growth Outliers (4 teams), and Historic Blue-Chip Franchises (39 teams).

plot15_pyspark_speedup.title: Distributed Scaling Speedup and Execution Runtime Benchmark
plot15_pyspark_speedup.inference: Empirical verification of distributed computing crossover dynamics: At 1x (N=50) and 10x (N=500), single-node Scikit-Learn outperforms PySpark (speedup 0.00x - 0.27x) due to JVM context initialization, Catalyst query planning, and RDD partition serialization overhead. However, between N=500 and N=5,000 (~1,800 records), computational workload crosses the parity threshold (1.0x). At 100x (N=5,000), PySpark achieves a 1.63x speedup, and at 1000x (N=50,000), it achieves a massive 5.20x speedup (13.82s vs 71.85s) by executing FP-Growth and Gaussian Naive Bayes across multi-core workers.
